 Vietnam's e-commerce market reached VND 442 trillion after 9 months, and the race is shifting towards high-value goods.
 In the first nine months of 2026, total sales across the four platforms Shopee, TikTok Shop, Lazada, and Tiki reached approximately 442 trillion VND, a 44.47% increase compared to the same period last year, while volume only increased by 12.46%. Average transaction value increased rapidly, the proportion of items priced over 1 million VND expanded, and the market share gap between Shopee and TikTok Shop narrowed significantly.
 Báo Pháp Luật Việt Nam • 28/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Sales increased by nearly 45%, while production only increased by 12%. 
 According to data from the Metric data aggregation and mining platform, the Vietnamese e-commerce market continued to maintain a high growth rate in the first nine months of 2026. Across the four platforms Shopee, Lazada, Tiki, and TikTok Shop, total sales reached approximately VND 442 trillion, an increase of 44.47% compared to the same period in 2025.
 Total sales volume reached 3,275.8 million products, an increase of 12.46%. The number of shops generating orders reached 661,200, an increase of 16.74%. The large gap between sales growth rate and volume indicates that the average transaction value in the market is increasing, rather than growth primarily driven by selling more low-priced products.
 Third quarter sets new sales milestone. 
 In the third quarter of 2026 alone, total sales across all four exchanges reached VND 150,400 billion, an increase of 45.16% compared to the same period last year. Sales volume reached 1,089.1 million products.
 During the quarter, the number of shops generating orders decreased slightly by 2.47%, to 470,300. However, sales still increased strongly, indicating a shift in the market's seller structure, with less efficient small businesses shrinking and well-established businesses accounting for a larger share. 
 One of the most notable points in the third quarter was the continued narrowing of the market share gap between Shopee and TikTok Shop. From a difference of nearly 15 percentage points in the same period of 2025, the gap between the two platforms is now just over 1 percentage point.
 TikTok Shop dominates the Men's and Women's Fashion categories. Meanwhile, Shopee leads in the Phones & Tablets, Home Appliances, and Home & Lifestyle groups. The two platforms are also directly competing in the Beauty, Groceries & Food, Sports & Travel, and Health categories.
 Shop Malls account for a small percentage but contribute a large portion of sales. 
 The sales concentration effect continues to be evident on e-commerce platforms. The Shop Mall group, while accounting for only 3.54% of the total number of stores, generates 36.8% of total sales on Shopee and TikTok Shop. This proportion demonstrates the growing role of official brand stores, especially for high-value products.
 Meanwhile, domestic sellers and warehouses account for the majority of sales on Shopee. This group contributes 95.6% of the platform's sales, up from 92.4% in the same period of 2025, equivalent to VND 69,800 billion.
 Conversely, sales from foreign sellers decreased by 27.1%, to VND 3,200 billion. Consequently, their share of the market fell from 7.6% to 4.4%.
 You may also like The shift in price segment structure is another notable aspect of the market. In Q3 2026, products priced under VND 200,000 accounted for 42.2% of total sales, a sharp decrease from 50.1% in the same period of the previous year. Conversely, all five segments priced at VND 200,000 and above recorded an increase in sales share. Most notably, the segment priced above VND 1 million saw its sales share increase from 14.5% to 19%.
 This trend shows that online consumers are expanding their spending to higher-value products. E-commerce is no longer primarily focused on low-priced items but is expanding into the mid- and high-end segments.
 The development of official retail outlets, along with increasingly clear consumer protection policies, is contributing to this trend. For businesses, the shift in pricing structure also poses new competitive challenges. As the proportion of products priced under 200,000 VND shrinks, the advantage of a low-price competitive strategy is no longer as pronounced as before. Instead, brand, product quality, delivery experience, and customer service become crucial factors in persuading consumers to choose higher-value products.
 Pet care: Sales increase despite decreased production. 
 In the third quarter of 2026, the Pet Care industry recorded sales of VND 1,921.5 billion, an increase of 38.2% compared to the same period in 2025. Notably, production volume decreased by 6.9%, to 22.9 million products. The number of shops also decreased by 9%, to 20,700 shops. 
 Sales increased while both production volume and the number of sellers decreased, indicating that the market is focusing more on professional sellers and product lines with higher transaction values. The two main product groups, Food and Accessories, achieved sales of VND 795 billion and VND 481.1 billion respectively, contributing approximately two-thirds of the total industry sales.
 The remaining groups include Other Pet Care at VND 231.3 billion, Hygiene at VND 183.5 billion, Healthcare at VND 121.8 billion, and Beauty at VND 99.8 billion.
 In terms of value, the product group priced under 200,000 VND still accounts for the largest share, at 58.2% of total sales.
 The pet care industry is characterized by repeat purchases, as food and essential products are used frequently. Consumers tend to split orders and prioritize convenience when shopping online. With prices under 200,000 VND, products in this category play a crucial role in maintaining purchase frequency and a stable revenue stream for sellers.
 Household electricity prices increased by over 51%. 
 Household appliances were among the top 5 fastest-growing sectors in Q3 2026. Sales reached VND 7,966.7 billion, a 51.4% increase compared to the same period last year. Production volume reached 22.8 million units, a 2.6% increase.
 While sales and production increased, the number of shops decreased by 13.9%, to 47,500. 
 You may also like Kitchen appliances and small household electrical equipment are the two main contributors, accounting for 65.2% of total industry sales. Meanwhile, circuits and components have a large volume of products sold but contribute significantly less to overall sales.
 Overall, products priced at 1 million VND or more contributed 57.7% of the household appliance industry's sales, even though the average value per product was only about 350,000 VND. The fact that no single price segment accounted for more than 27% of sales indicates that the industry's purchasing power is relatively widely distributed, ranging from mass-market products to higher-value items.
 The fourth quarter is expected to continue accelerating. 
 According to Metric's forecast, sales on the four e-commerce platforms in Q4 2026 could reach VND 165.5 trillion, with approximately 1,102.3 million products sold. Compared to Q3, sales are expected to increase by 10.05%, while volume will increase by 1.22%. Year-end promotional programs such as 11/11, 12/12, Christmas, and the pre-New Year shopping season are expected to provide further impetus to the market. Demand is projected to be concentrated in the Beauty, Fashion, Electronics, Home Appliances, and Gift categories.
 Besides discount programs, short video sales, livestreaming, and flexible promotional programs tailored to specific times continue to be used to increase conversion rates and compete for market share in the year-end period.
 With projected sales of VND 165.5 trillion in the fourth quarter, the Vietnamese e-commerce market is expected to continue its growth momentum, with the value of goods and consumer spending patterns remaining key factors to watch.
